title: Regionized KV allocation with aging compaction and batch-aware placement
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement a region-based KV allocation strategy paired with an aging-driven opportunistic compaction mechanism and batch-aware placement heuristics. Goals: reduce long-term fragmentation, minimize tail latency impact from compaction, and improve GPU memory utilization under continuous batching workloads.
background: Current slab+slot allocators work well for steady-state loads but fragment over long-lived sessions and mixed-size KV entries. Continuous batching amplifies fragmentation because requests with varying sequence lengths and KV lifetimes interleave. Prior tickets have explored slab tiers and generational compaction, but we observe recurring small free segments that are hard to reclaim without service-impacting pauses.
proposed_solution: 1) Partition KV pool into regions: hot (frequently read/extended), warm (medium lifetime), cold (long-lived/pinned), and transient (short-lived). 2) Allocate new keys into transient/hot based on a lightweight lifetime prediction (sequence length + batch-size heuristic). 3) Maintain an atomic per-region free-list and a compacting thread that performs incremental coalescing and memcpy-based slot consolidation when GPU load is low or under soft watermarks. 4) Batch-aware placement: prefer placing entries from the same request/batch contiguously to reduce scatter during KV eviction and to improve contiguous memcpy efficiency during compaction. 5) Aging counters: keep per-entry age buckets sampled at allocation time to drive region promotion/demotion and to make compaction targets more deterministic. 6) Throttle compaction work using SLO-aware tokens to avoid impacting tail latency. 7) Expose runtime telemetry and an operator knob to favor space efficiency vs. latency (aggressive vs conservative compaction modes).
milestones: M1: Design doc and microbench library for regionized allocator (design + perf harness) - 2026-03-08
M2: Prototype allocation policy + microbench results (hot/warm/cold placements) - 2026-03-22
M4: Integrate batch-aware placement into request router and run end-to-end perf tests - 2026-04-05
M5: Gradual rollout to canary cluster with telemetry and fallback - 2026-04-12
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with serving and scheduler teams. Agreed on region definitions and initial telemetry metrics.
2026-03-05: Prototype allocator data structures implemented in the runtime test harness. Initial microbench shows 12% lower fragmentation on synthetic churn workloads.
2026-03-09: Design review complete. Feedback: make compactor preemption-friendly and add deterministic sampling for age buckets. Action: add per-stream compaction quotas.

2026-03-12: First end-to-end run with batch-aware placement enabled. Observed improved memcpy locality but a small 0.8% increase in median token latency under max load; will add rate limiting to compaction threads.
open_questions: How to best predict entry lifetime with minimal CPU overhead? (current plan: sequence-length heuristic + batch-size proxy)
Should pinned/privileged entries be allowed inside hot region mappings or be forcibly placed in cold/pinned region?
Trade-off curve we expose to customers for aggressive compaction vs tail latency — what defaults should enterprise vs dev tiers get?
decisions: Adopt regionized pool (hot/warm/cold/transient) instead of expanding slab strata to avoid frequent slab migrations.
Implement incremental memcpy-based compaction limited by SLO tokens to prevent compaction from causing tail spikes.
Place entries from the same batch contiguously when possible; fall back to best-fit when constraints prevent contiguous placement.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end canary demonstrates >=20% reduction in reclaimable fragmentation vs current baseline over a 48h churn workload
99th percentile token latency impact from compaction remains within 3% of baseline under production load
Telemetry surfaces region-level fragmentation, compaction bytes moved, compaction CPU/GPU time, and SLO token usage
Feature has a safe rollback path and a runtime knob to revert to legacy allocator without requiring model restarts
